name: Rodrigo Duterte
summary: Duterte governed on law-and-order populism: a drug war carried out through mass police killings, Mindanao martial law and the Anti-Terrorism Act, alongside pressure on critics and the press. He also signed free tuition and universal health care laws, pushed to restore the death penalty and a federal constitution, and moved toward China while keeping the US alliance.

universal-healthcare.rationale: He approved the Universal Health Care Act on 20 February 2019, enrolling every Filipino in national health insurance.

regulate-corporations.rationale: In 2016 he backed his environment secretary's suspension of mining permits and said mining must be limited even when legal; this rests on 2016-2017 statements only.

surveillance-ok.rationale: He approved the Anti-Terrorism Act of 2020, which authorises court-ordered wiretapping and 14-day warrantless detention of terror suspects.

legalize-drugs.rationale: His administration's central policy was a violent crackdown on drug users and sellers, with threats such as 'if you go into drugs... I will kill you'.

empower-police-military.rationale: He told troops 'I have your backs', ordered Mindanao martial law and signed the Anti-Terrorism Act expanding security-force powers.

decide-locally.rationale: He created the Consultative Committee by EO 10 and endorsed its 18-region federal draft in his 2018 address.

same-sex-marriage.rationale: In 2016 he said he would not push to legalize it, holding marriage to be between a man and a woman under the Civil Code.

abortion-legal.rationale: He said he would not tolerate abortion because a human being is already in the womb, and repeated 'I am not for abortion' in 2017.

limit-population.rationale: He signed an order to end unmet need for modern family planning but said 'I am not for birth control' and nothing records a goal of limiting population.

security-forces-accountable.rationale: He withdrew the Philippines from the ICC when it examined his drug-war killings, and HRW found almost no prosecutions of officers; he had promised police protection.

emergency-suspend-protections.rationale: He proclaimed martial law in Mindanao and suspended the writ of habeas corpus on 23 May 2017 to defeat the Maute rebellion, and defended it as the fastest way to quell it.

unlimited-reelection.rationale: The draft constitution he commissioned and endorsed allows one re-election of the president, and at his request barred him from the 2022 race.

end-foreign-alliances.rationale: He gave notice ending the US Visiting Forces Agreement in February 2020 but suspended it three times and recalled it in July 2021, so his record points both ways.

death-penalty.rationale: He asked Congress in his 2017 and 2019 State of the Nation Addresses to reinstate the death penalty for heinous drug crimes (and plunder in 2019), calling it retribution as well as deterrence; it never passed.

no-fault-divorce.rationale: As a candidate he opposed divorce, saying it injures families.

suppress-opposition.rationale: HRW reports opposition Senator de Lima jailed, sedition complaints against the vice president, red-tagging of activists and his campaign against ABS-CBN, Rappler and the Inquirer.

stay-neutral-between-blocs.rationale: He announced a 'separation' from the US in Beijing and a China-Russia bloc, yet said alliances would stay and restored the VFA, so his record points both ways.

term-limits.rationale: At his request the federal draft barred the incumbent president from running in 2022 and kept a four-year term renewable once.

free-public-college.rationale: He approved the Universal Access to Quality Tertiary Education Act on 3 August 2017, making state university tuition free.

international-criminal-courts.rationale: He pulled the Philippines out of the Rome Statute in March 2018, calling the ICC a political tool against the Philippines.

minority-territorial-autonomy.rationale: He signed the Bangsamoro Organic Law on 26 July 2018, creating a self-governing region for the Muslim minority-majority areas of Mindanao.

extrajudicial-killing.rationale: Police killings of suspected drug users and dealers ran through his presidency under his orders (HRW quotes 'My order is shoot to kill you' and a promise to protect officers who kill); police reported 5,526 suspects killed in three years.

close-ties-china.rationale: In October 2016 he went to Beijing, signed 13 agreements and took over $9bn in Chinese loans, and chose bilateral talks over pressing the arbitration win.

labour-priority-over-capital.rationale: He vetoed the 2019 anti-contractualization bill, saying it upset the balance between business and workers and that security of tenure must not harm employers.

avoid-permanent-military-alliances.rationale: He said in September 2016 'We are not cutting our alliances', and he kept the US security arrangements, restoring the Visiting Forces Agreement in 2021.

notes: Researched theme by theme: security and drugs, rule of law and courts, press, economy and labour, social issues, foreign policy, federalism and term limits, environment and mining. Official Gazette, Inquirer, Rappler, Reuters and the ICC site were blocked or unavailable, and the UN General Assembly speeches in the local UNGDC corpus (2016-2018) were delivered by foreign secretaries, not Duterte, so they were not used. Statements he is reported to have changed his mind on (same-sex marriage, Paris Agreement, mining) were answered only from sources opened; a later position is not assumed. Where he has a record (martial law, laws signed, ICC withdrawal, VFA) the record answers and his words are left out.
